text:
alice: Customer reported 500 errors + apparent duplicate billing after they upgraded to python-sdk 2.0 this morning. They say requests that used to be idempotent are showing as two successful calls. They pinned back to 1.9.x and that stopped the doubles. Any ideas?

support-lina: Oof. Do we have logs or a repro? Which endpoint and which method?

alice: Sent sample trace from customer (attached). They call `client.generate()` with `timeout_ms=60000` and our older SDK honored it. After 2.0 their client ignored `timeout_ms` (no error) and retried on timeout at app layer. The server saw two in-flight requests. Customer says they saw two invoice lines.

devex-mike: Quick check: 2.0 removed some legacy kwargs and unified timeouts to `timeout` (seconds) in the constructor. We added a deprecation but apparently it no longer raises or logs. That's bad.

eng-jordan: Can you paste the exact snippet they used? Also thread the request IDs from the server logs, I can check routing.

alice: Their snippet: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., timeout_ms=60000)
resp = client.generate(prompt)
```

eng-jordan: Thanks. So `timeout_ms` was silently ignored instead of triggering a fallback. That explains the app-layer retry. We should treat that as a breaking change and either reintroduce compatibility or make the change raise an explicit error.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollback-py-sdk-2.0-compat-shim -> staging

support-lina: Customer asks for recommended pinned version and a mitigation while we sort this. Billing impacted: two charges per request.

billing-zoe: If duplicates were caused by our SDK change we should escalate for refund. Need customer request IDs and timestamps to match invoices. I can fast-track credits once Eng confirms root cause.

devex-mike: Short-term mitigation: instruct customers to pin to `redwood-sdk==1.9.8` (last known behaviour) OR change their code to use `timeout` in seconds: `RedwoodClient(timeout=60)`. But because `timeout_ms` currently silently drops, we should add a patch that maps `timeout_ms` -> `timeout` and logs a warning.

alice: I'll tell the customer to pin to 1.9.8 and provide the `timeout` migration snippet. Also asking for receipts to pass to billing.

customer-james: Thanks — pinned and it fixed the duplicates for now. Sending two invoice ids and three request IDs from our service.

eng-jordan: I'll add a hotfix PR to reintroduce a compatibility layer that maps `timeout_ms` to `timeout` and emits a clear warning. Also adding a test to fail loudly if unknown kwargs are passed.

devex-mike: Can we also backport to 1.9.x as a safety? Or push a 2.0.1 compatibility patch. We should avoid forcing immediate rollback for everyone.

eng-jordan: Plan: 1) open PR for 2.0.1 compat shim (map `timeout_ms` and `max_wait_ms` to new names, warn), 2) add unit + integration tests for idsempotency on retries, 3) confirm refunds with billing. If accepted, release patch within 24h.

billing-zoe: I'll prepare credit once request IDs are validated. Send along customer receipts and timestamps.

support-lina: Logging/observability ask: add a metric for "ignored kwargs" so we can catch silent drops in future.

eng-jordan: Good call. I'll add a telemetry event when unexpected kwargs are detected.

alice: Summary for customer: pin to `redwood-sdk==1.9.8` OR update constructor to `timeout=60`, we are rolling a 2.0.1 patch to re-enable `timeout_ms` mapping and will follow up with credits once billing validates. Sorry for the disruption.

devex-mike: Also adding a short doc note in migration guide and a CLI lint that flags deprecated kwargs during `pip install`/import.

customer-james: Appreciate it, thanks for the fast response.

alice: Marking this escalated -> eng-priority. @eng-jordan can you post PR link when ready? :thumbsup:
